rule: Spring tides bloom salt-bloom in the tide-pools
texts: When a spring tide fills the tide-pools, salt-bloom blooms in the tide-pools.
If a spring tide fills the tide-pools, salt-bloom grows in the tide-pools.
Salt-bloom is a pale crystalline crust.
The bloom soon dissolves into the seawater.

fields.sentence: Spring tides bloom salt-bloom in the tide-pools

q1_issues.issue: Both arguments are bare kind-denoting NPs ('spring tides', 'salt-bloom'), which is the stated trigger for a kind-level relational generic ((Bloom spring_tide salt_bloom), explicitly 'not a per-instance rule'), yet the parse emits the distributing per-instance Implication.

q2_gaps: a bare-kind relational generic that also carries an oblique ('in the tide-pools'): the kind-level relation is an opaque two-argument atom with no slot for a locative, and the instruction set never says which form wins when the relational-generic trigger fires on a clause with obliques
review_run1.notes: Everything else matches the instruction set: genus-only decomposition of the three noun-modifier compounds, the definite plural as a top-level group witness referenced from inside the rule (the 'Foxes rarely cross the causeway' shape), a bare class symbol for the non-specific object, 0.9/0.9 for the bare generic, and no tense atom.

fields.sentence: When a spring tide fills the tide-pools, salt-bloom blooms in the tide-pools.
parse_run2: (: fx84_rule (Implication (And (Member $e fill) (Member $t spring_tide) (Agent $e $t) (Patient $e sk_tide_pool_1)) (And (Member (sk_bloom $e) bloom) (Member (sk_saltbloom $e) salt_bloom) (Patient (sk_bloom $e) (sk_saltbloom $e)) (Location (sk_bloom $e) sk_tide_pool_1) (During (sk_bloom $e) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: "a spring tide" is an indefinite, but the premise fills Agent with the bare kind symbol spring_tide; an indefinite argument is an existential (witness + class atom), and inside a rule premise it binds as a variable plus (Member $t spring_tide) — as written the premise can never match an actual filling event, whose Agent would be a witness symbol.

q2_gaps: Generic conditional headed by bare "when" ("When <clause>, <clause>"): "when" is listed among the temporal connectives that keep their canonical time forms, while the occurrence-quantifying Implication form is specified only for "every time / whenever" and "if"; which route a habitual "when"-clause takes is never stated.

Zero-derived noun/verb homonymy: the substance's decomposition genus (Inheritance salt_bloom bloom) and the event class (Member <e> bloom) land on one symbol, making the substance a subkind of the event class. The instruction set rules on derivation across parts of speech but says nothing about a noun and a verb that share a base form.
review_run1.notes: Definite-plural handling is right: "the tide-pools" gets a top-level group witness and both mentions reuse it; the compound genera correctly withhold the noun modifiers tide / spring / salt. Patient for "fills the tide-pools", Patient for the intransitive blooming, Location for "in", and the During tie to the trigger all follow the instruction set.

fields.sentence: If a spring tide fills the tide-pools, salt-bloom grows in the tide-pools.
parse_run2: (: tide_grow_rule (Implication (And (Member $f fill) (Agent $f $t) (Member $t spring_tide) (Patient $f sk_group_1)) (And (Member (sk_grow $f) grow) (Patient (sk_grow $f) salt_bloom) (Location (sk_grow $f) sk_group_1) (During (sk_grow $f) $f))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The consequent event is keyed only to the tide, `(sk_grow $t)`, although the fill event `$e1` is bound in the premise and scopes over it too; per the Skolem-function rule a dependent existential is a function of every universal scoping over it, so as written two fillings by one spring tide yield a single grow event.

review_run1.notes: Everything else checks out: indicative conditional as a plain Implication rule, definite plural "the tide-pools" as a group witness shared by both clauses, all three compound genera emitted with their noun modifiers unexposed, Agent on the inanimate transitive subject, Patient on the change-of-state intransitive subject, and Location on the growing event.

fields.sentence: Salt-bloom is a pale crystalline crust.

q1_issues.issue: The fused compound kind salt_bloom is used without its decomposition genus (Inheritance salt_bloom bloom), which the compound-kind rule requires (the head-noun genus is always emitted); the only Inheritance given to a genus position is the copular predicate 'crust'.

review_run1.notes: Kind subject taking Inheritance and the split of the descriptive 'pale' / 'crystalline' from the head noun (no adjective-noun fusion) are correct. The definitional 0.99 confidence is defensible for a defining copular, though 'pale' would take the empirical 0.9 if read as contingent.

fields.sentence: The bloom soon dissolves into the seawater.

q2_gaps: the proximate-future adverb 'soon': it is not one of the named speech-anchored deictic constants (yesterday/tonight/next_summer/...) and no other carrier is specified for it, so its content is dropped — its only trace here is the `Future` atom; the instruction set also does not say whether 'soon' counts as the 'lexically future adjunct' that licenses the present-tense futurate (the listed examples are 'tomorrow / next week / in two days')
review_run1.notes: Roles and typing are right — `Patient` for the change-of-state intransitive 'dissolve', `Goal` for the whither-'into' path, article-bearing 'the seawater' minting a witness with its kind atom. The one contestable atom is `Future`, which stands or falls on whether 'soon' is a lexically future adjunct.
